evidence_items.value: Patient with history of intellectual disability and epilepsy, first seizure at age 5, severe intellectual disability with limited communication. EEG showed focal theta activity in left posterior temporal-occipital area. MRI showed punctate T2/FLAIR subcortical white matter hyperintensities. Seizure types include generalized tonic-clonic. Medications: valproic acid and lamotrigine. Responded well to broad-spectrum antiepileptic drugs.

raw_source.text_snippet: A 35-year-old female was initially seen in clinic in April 2023 for epilepsy. She had a history of intellectual disability and epilepsy and had moved from Venezuela to Iowa, USA. She had her first seizure at five years of age. She and her mother are Spanish-speaking. The patient has severe intellectual disability and only limited communication capability. Her records, which were available in Spanish, were translated and reviewed. She had an electroencephalogram (EEG) done in 2018 in Venezuela, which showed focal bursts of paroxysmal theta activity in the left posterior temporal-occipital area. As this EEG was done in Venezuela, records of EEG waveforms were not available. An EEG done at our center in May 2023 was a normal awake EEG but was limited due to electrode and muscle artifacts. She had magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain done in the USA, which did not show any epileptogenic lesions. MRI brain findings (Figures 1, 2) showed a few incidental punctate T2 and FLAIR subcortical white matter hyperintensities. She has been on valproic acid 500 mg three times a day. Her last seizure was in March 2023. She has exhibited different seizure semiologies, including generalized tonic-clonic type events. Because of her intellectual disability and epilepsy, she was referred to genetics.

PCGF2 plays a role in regulating the differentiation of cardiac mesoderm. Loss of PCGF2 function has been shown to downregulate PTEN, leading to enhanced AKT activation, increased HIF-1α levels, and upregulation of VEGF.
